title: Bram and the Contact
premise: Tamsin Nystrom has spent a decade erasing herself on behalf of the Meridian Group, a deniable intelligence outfit buried inside diplomatic paperwork. When a routine cleanup job hands her a dead man's voiceprint, she uses it to open a server holding proof that the Group's founder engineered a massacre to protect an inheritance he never legally owned. Pursued by the Group's assassin and disavowed by every government she once served, Tamsin allies with Bram, a disgraced archivist who keeps the Group's true records, to smuggle the evidence to a tribunal that has already been bought. In the end she trades her own anonymity for the truth, testifying under her real name and letting the Group burn, knowing justice outside the law cost her the only life she knew how to live.
about_author: Edmund Ravensworth is the pen name of a former diplomatic archivist who spent fifteen years cataloguing documents he was never allowed to read. He writes thrillers from a coastal town whose location he declines to confirm.

chapters.title: The Unattributable
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. In Vienna, she quietly destroys evidence tying a minister to a bribery ring, showcasing her craft and her creed: exist nowhere, owe no one. Her handler, Voss, assigns one last cleanup involving a dead courier. The emotional beat is professional detachment masking a growing unease that the Group is tidying up people, not just paper.

chapters.title: A Dead Man's Voice
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Sorting the courier's effects, she finds a voiceprint key and, against protocol, plays it into a locked server in Singapore. It opens. The files name the Meridian Group's founder and a massacre in Tallinn dressed as an accident. The emotional beat is the vertigo of a woman who realizes she has been the eraser, not the archivist.

chapters.title: The Archivist's Debt
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Introduced in a flooded basement archive in Riga, Bram is a former Group records-keeper who kept copies of everything as insurance. Tamsin arrives asking the wrong questions; he recognizes her as the woman who erased his brother's file years ago. The beat is wary, hostile alliance: he'll help, but only to settle a debt she doesn't remember owing.

chapters.title: Three Governments, One Lie
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Tamsin and Bram trace how Tallinn's cover-up was co-signed by intelligence services in three countries, each protecting a founder who is now a revered statesman. Voss summons Tamsin home; she smells the trap and refuses. The beat is betrayal sharpening into resolve as she understands the law itself is the conspirator.

chapters.title: The Quiet Professional
chapters.summary: Assassin Ilse's POV. The Group activates its cleaner: Ilse, who has killed for them for twenty years and believes in the work. She closes in on Riga, and Tamsin barely escapes a staged gas explosion. The beat is cold dread, the first time Tamsin is the thing being erased, hunted by someone who is very good at it.

chapters.title: What Bram Kept
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. On the run through the Baltics, Bram reveals the full archive: ledgers proving the founder's fortune was stolen from a murdered heir, the inheritance at the story's rotten heart. Tamsin realizes the courier was the heir's grandchild. The beat is grief transmuted into purpose; the case has become personal for both of them.

chapters.title: The Bought Tribunal
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Their planned venue, an international tribunal in The Hague, is revealed to be compromised: the presiding judge took the Group's money decades ago. Desperate, Tamsin contacts a journalist she once ruined, offering the archive as penance. The beat is humility, a fixer learning she can't fix this one alone or off the books.

chapters.title: Ilse's Doubt
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. Ordered to kill Bram and Tamsin and burn the archive, Ilse reads the Tallinn files to confirm her target list and finds her own sister's name among the dead. She stalls, then turns, feeding the Group false confirmation. The beat is a killer's crisis of faith; the instrument of power discovers it was also its victim.

chapters.title: The Long Handover
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Climax: a midnight handover in a Rotterdam freight yard goes wrong when Voss arrives in person, revealing he built the Group's deniability and intends to inherit it himself. Ilse holds him off while Bram and Tamsin transmit the archive to forty newsrooms simultaneously. Voss dies by his own contingency, and the truth is loose and unstoppable.

chapters.title: A Name, Spoken Aloud
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV, coda. Weeks later, the statesman resigns, tribunals reopen, and Tamsin testifies under her real name, surrendering the invisibility that was her entire identity. She and Bram visit the courier's grave in Tallinn. The beat is bittersweet resolution: justice achieved outside the law, paid for with the self she used to be, and somehow worth it.
